Judgment calls: (a) OFF-FRAME COMPONENT - Resistor 2 (4k) bbox is (185.2,7.3) w69.3 h36.1, i.e. y from -10.8 to +25.4, and a row-by-row pixel scan shows image rows 0-12 are COMPLETELY blank: the resistor symbol was cut away by the preprocessing crop and is not drawn at all. The only two bare wire ends in the whole drawing are at (153,13) - the right end of the top horizontal - and (271,13) - the top of Inductor 1's lead; the resistor's bbox spans x 151-220 horizontally between/above them, so it is inferred to bridge those two stubs. That also completes the only loop the inductor could otherwise not participate in, and leaves no dangling lead anywhere. (b) The 4-way at (123,242) where the left rail crosses the GND stem / middle horizontal is read as a JUNCTION: the GND stem visibly terminates there (nothing left of the three ground bars at x=82/90/100), and if it were a crossover, net 0 would be just GND plus one capacitor plate with no return path, and the whole outer loop would float. (c) The inductor's bottom lead terminates ON the middle horizontal at (287,233) - verified in the pixel map, no ink below y=236 at that x - so it is a T-junction, not a crossing. (d) The right rail overshoots ~5px above the corner at (418,221) and the left rail runs a few px past the top-left corner; both are pen overshoots, not connections. (e) V-AC 6 carries no polarity marks (just a '~'), so its terminal order is arbitrary: index 0 = left lead (net 0), index 1 = right lead (n4). (f) Capacitors 0 and 4 are indexed left plate = 0, right plate = 1; Resistor 5 and Inductor 1 top = 0, bottom = 1. (g) The bootstrap had Resistor 5 index 1 on '0' - that is wrong: the bottom rail is split by V-AC 6, so only the piece LEFT of the source is ground; the piece right of it (n4) carries the resistor's bottom lead. Inductor 1's bootstrap nets n1/n2 happened to be right and were kept.
